results.text: 31 Global Poverty: Stalled Pro GreSS and riSinG Con Centration (refer to annex 1B, figure 1B.2). results.text: 22 POVERTY , PROSPERITY , AND PLANET REPORT 2026 in 2000 to a majority by 2026, and extreme poverty has all but disappeared. In today’s lower-middle-income economies, the group living on between $3.00 and $8.30 a day is now the largest, and the middle class, though growing, remains a minority. results.text: The thresholds used in this report can serve as approximate class boundaries. Each of the three poverty lines is the typical national poverty line of an income group: $3.00 a day for low-income economies, $4.20 for lower-middle-income economies, and $8.30 for upper-middle-income economies (refer to box 1.1). Households living on less than $3.00 a day are extremely poor by any standard. Those living on between $3.00 and $8.30 are above the extreme poverty line, but would count as poor in a middle-income economy and, for the most part, remain short of economic security. Those living on between $8.30 and $28.00 a day are above the poverty line of every developing economy and constitute a global middle class; and those above $28.00 a day exceed the prosperity standard this report uses to gauge shared prosperity (refer to chapter 2). In low-income economies, the distribution has barely shifted. About half the population is still living on less than $3.00 a day, and the middle class is negligible. High-income economies, by contrast, are composed almost entirely of households living on more than $8.30 a day, and the majority are above the prosperity standard.

metadata.section: Gains in global poverty reduction could be reversed in coming decades

context_chunks.text: The thresholds used in this report can serve as approximate class boundaries. Each of the three poverty lines is the typical national poverty line of an income group: $3.00 a day for low-income economies, $4.20 for lower-middle-income economies, and $8.30 for upper-middle-income economies (refer to box 1.1). Households living on less than $3.00 a day are extremely poor by any standard. Those living on between $3.00 and $8.30 are above the extreme poverty line, but would count as poor in a middle-income economy and, for the most part, remain short of economic security. Those living on between $8.30 and $28.00 a day are above the poverty line of every developing economy and constitute a global middle class; and those above $28.00 a day exceed the prosperity standard this report uses to gauge shared prosperity (refer to chapter 2). answer: Theo phân loại gần đúng của báo cáo, nhóm trung lưu toàn cầu sống với thu nhập hoặc tiêu dùng khoảng từ 8,30 USD đến 28,00 USD mỗi ngày. Ngưỡng 8,30 USD là đường nghèo điển hình của nền kinh tế thu nhập trung lưu bậc trên, còn 28,00 USD là chuẩn thịnh vượng mà báo cáo dùng để đo thịnh vượng chung.
